shorts.title: Why iron kills the biggest stars
shorts.question: What actually makes a giant star explode?
minimumContext: giant stars stay alive by fusing ever-heavier elements in their core
shorts.payoff: iron fusion costs energy, the core collapses in under a second and rebounds into a supernova

delta.openingLine: A giant star holds itself up against its own gravity by fusing heavier and heavier elements in its core. Until it reaches iron.
delta.closingLine: And what's left behind can become a black hole.
delta.portraitRestage: onion and core diagrams stacked full-width; labels above and below

shorts.title: You are made of exploded stars
shorts.question: Where did the oxygen and calcium in your body come from?
minimumContext: a supernova is a giant star exploding
shorts.payoff: NASA: all the Solar System's oxygen, about half its calcium and ~40% of its iron came from exploding massive stars

delta.openingLine: The oxygen in your next breath came from exploding stars.
delta.closingLine: And oxygen alone is about two thirds of your body's weight.
delta.portraitRestage: Chandra image top, colour key below; bars full-width

shorts.title: The moment a star switches on
shorts.question: What turns a cloud of gas into a shining star?
minimumContext: stars form inside cold clouds of gas and dust
shorts.payoff: at about fifteen million degrees hydrogen fuses into helium: a star is born

delta.openingLine: Every star begins inside a cold, dark cloud of gas and dust, where the gas gathers into dense clumps.
delta.portraitRestage: illustrations recomposed tall; temperature readout centred

shorts.title: How do you find something invisible?
shorts.question: If black holes give off no light, how do we find them?
minimumContext: no light escapes a black hole
shorts.payoff: by their pull on companion stars: Cygnus X-1 (~21 Suns) glows in X-rays; Gaia BH3 (~33 Suns) was found by a wobble

delta.openingLine: Nothing escapes a black hole, not even light.

shorts.title: The giant star that vanished
shorts.question: Can a giant star turn into a black hole without exploding?
minimumContext: most giant stars die in a supernova explosion
shorts.payoff: N6946-BH1 flared weakly and seemed to vanish; a failed supernova is one explanation, still debated

delta.openingLine: Most giant stars die in a huge explosion. But maybe not all of them.
delta.closingLine: If the failed-supernova idea is confirmed, astronomers say it would be the first time anyone has seen a black hole being born.

shorts.title: Why giant stars die young
shorts.question: Why do heavier stars live shorter lives?

delta.openingLine: The biggest stars live the shortest lives.

shorts.rejectedReason: two diagram scenes give a fact but no complete visual explanation or payoff a stranger would feel; five stronger Shorts exist
